## Welcome

This site contains documentation, tutorials, and analyses for spacecraft simulations using the [Basilisk](https://hanspeterschaub.info/basilisk/) astrodynamics framework.

Basilisk is an open-source spacecraft simulation framework developed by the University of Colorado Boulder's Autonomous Vehicle Systems Lab. It provides high-fidelity modeling of:

- Orbital dynamics
- Attitude dynamics and control
- Power systems
- Communication systems
- Sensor and actuator models
- Hardware-in-the-loop testing

## Getting Started

### Tutorials

Explore these tutorials to learn Basilisk fundamentals:

- **[Basic Orbit Scenario](docs/main/scenarioBasicOrbit.html)** - Learn how to set up orbital simulations with different gravity models and orbit types

### Installation

To run these simulations yourself:

1. Clone the [Basilisk repository](https://github.com/AVSLab/basilisk)
2. Follow the [installation instructions](https://hanspeterschaub.info/basilisk/Install/installOnMacOS.html)
3. Install required Python packages: `pip install numpy matplotlib jupyter`

## About

These tutorials demonstrate practical applications of Basilisk for spacecraft mission analysis and design. Each tutorial includes:

- Detailed explanations of the simulation setup
- Fully executable Python code
- Visualizations and analysis of results
- References for further learning
